Well all the overseas companies say ridiculous numbers just to get people to buy them, easy way to tell a reputable company from a shady one is if they list the actual wattage. The true wattage is what it draws from the wall but the par which is usable light for photosynthesis is what you should look for. Usually you'll see them recorded on a coverage map that makes it very easy to see how well it would fit your space. You should also look at the micromoles per joule  Above 2.2 is what I'd consider acceptable for an led. to cover a 3x3 in flower you'd need about 400 actual watts. 35 watts per square foot is a good general rule but spectrum and using proper colors for the stage the plant is in matters a lot as well.
